newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace urges Shell to end Atlantic exploration.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace urges Shell to end Atlantic exploration.

text.p: Greenpeace on Wednesday called on the Royal Dutch/Shell Group to abandon oil exploration in the north east of the Atlantic Ocean.
The environmental lobby group argues that any exploration west of Scotland's Shetland islands would be illegal and irresponsible.

Greenpeace, which succeeded two years ago in forcing Shell to abandon plans to sink-off the Brent Spar oil platform, also called for a permanent ban on further oil exploration to prevent "irreparable damage" to the climate.

"Shell tries to present themselves as taking a more environmental or sustainable approach to their work, while at the same time blatantly ignoring the impact of their product on the climate," Sarah Burton, a Greenpeace director, wrote in a letter to Shell.
The letter is the latest in a string of activist protests against Shell's environmental and human rights record in the run-up to the group's shareholders meetings later on Wednesday.
Greenpeace, meanwhile, expressed its support for a rebel shareholder resolution calling for an external environmental audit of Shell's activities.
Most of lobby groups' criticism focuses on Shell's activities in Nigeria following the execution of minority rights activists there in 1995.
